findings.summary: Eddyline achieves lower MAE than Brenna-ODE on the Kestrel-Grid test split (0.212 vs 0.219), with substantially lower NFE (17.8 vs 64) and lower latency (112 ms vs 241 ms per batch of 256).
findings.scope: Kestrel-Grid test split, 8,760 hourly forecast windows from 320 substations, MAE in normalized load units, NFE per window, latency in ms per batch of 256 on Halden H5 accelerator.
findings.caveats: No statistical tests reported; differences are descriptive only. Latency measured on one accelerator with batch size 256.

findings.summary: Eddyline also shows lower MAE than the reference non-ODE forecaster Sluice-TCN (0.212 vs 0.231) but higher latency (112 ms vs 38 ms per batch of 256).
findings.scope: Kestrel-Grid test split, MAE in normalized load units, latency in ms per batch of 256 on Halden H5 accelerator.
findings.caveats: No statistical tests reported; differences are descriptive only. Sluice-TCN has no NFE reported.

findings.summary: Eddyline's efficiency gain over Brenna-ODE is consistent across both NFE and latency, but the accuracy gain is small in absolute terms (0.007 MAE).
findings.scope: Kestrel-Grid test split, MAE, NFE, latency as above.
findings.caveats: No statistical tests; practical importance of the MAE difference is not established.

sentences.text: On the Kestrel-Grid test split, Eddyline achieved lower MAE than Brenna-ODE (0.212 vs 0.219) while using substantially fewer function evaluations (17.8 vs 64 NFE per window) and lower latency (112 ms vs 241 ms per batch of 256).
Eddyline also outperformed the reference non-ODE forecaster Sluice-TCN in MAE (0.212 vs 0.231), but at higher latency (112 ms vs 38 ms per batch of 256).
The efficiency advantage of Eddyline over Brenna-ODE was consistent across both NFE and latency, although the absolute MAE improvement was small (0.007).
